correctness.rationale: At c<1, T^p=cU^p contracts and the unique bounded solution of d[n+1]=Td[n]+e[n] is the forward Green series; at c>1 use the inverse Green series. Hilbert duality converts its l-infinity input norm into sup_{||v||=1} sum ||(T*)^j v||; residue classes reduce this exactly to simplex sums of sqrt weighted masses. For p=3, increasing sqrt(A)+sqrt(B) cannot attain a strict maximum inside a nondegenerate 2D triangle; checking all three boundary segments and the unique opposing-slope stationary point yields the radical. Independently differentiated F(t)=sqrt(1+99t)+sqrt(100-399t/4) and verified t=1724711/3489255, the exact radical and its strict improvement over the best one-residue bound 24. This is an infinite-dimensional argument, not a finite-grid extrapolation.
